# What each KVM selftest is expected to do, per vendor.
#
#   <test>  <vendor>  <pass|skip|fail>  <reason>
#
# Anything that comes out differently fails the run.  That is the whole
# point: "PVM does not support this" is a fact worth recording once and
# then holding still, and an unexplained change in either direction --
# something that starts failing, or something that starts passing -- is
# news.
#
# Delete an entry when the gap closes.  Do not edit one to match a new
# result without understanding why it changed.
#
# Measured on 2026-09-09 against v7.3-rc2 + the PVM port, in L1 on an
# i9-13900HK.  Every PVM row was taken with the kvm-intel row beside it,
# because a test that behaves identically under both vendors is telling
# us about the testbed rather than about PVM.

# --- passes under both.  These are the ones carrying real signal. ------
dirty_log_test			pvm	pass	shadow MMU write tracking
dirty_log_test			intel	pass
kvm_binary_stats_test		pvm	pass	stats plumbing
kvm_binary_stats_test		intel	pass
kvm_create_max_vcpus		pvm	pass	vCPU lifetime
kvm_create_max_vcpus		intel	pass
kvm_page_table_test		pvm	pass	shadow MMU
kvm_page_table_test		intel	pass
memslot_modification_stress_test pvm	pass	memslot churn, which PVM pins the PVCS against
memslot_modification_stress_test intel	pass
x86/debug_regs			pvm	pass	DR handling through the switcher
x86/debug_regs			intel	pass
x86/max_vcpuid_cap_test		pvm	pass
x86/max_vcpuid_cap_test		intel	pass
x86/state_test			pvm	pass	vCPU state round trip
x86/state_test			intel	pass
x86/sync_regs_test		pvm	pass	KVM_SYNC_X86_REGS against the switcher's save/restore
x86/sync_regs_test		intel	pass

# --- fails under both: the testbed, not PVM ---------------------------
# "MMIO during vectoring error handling" wants KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR and
# gets KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN.  It does this under kvm-intel too, where L1 is
# itself a nested guest, so this says nothing about PVM.  Worth revisiting
# if the harness ever runs on bare metal.
set_memory_region_test		pvm	fail	fails identically under kvm-intel: nesting artefact
set_memory_region_test		intel	fail	same

# --- declared PVM gaps ------------------------------------------------
# PVM advertises neither capability, so the tests skip themselves rather
# than failing.  Both are known and listed in docs/STATUS.md.
pre_fault_memory_test		pvm	skip	no KVM_CAP_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY
pre_fault_memory_test		intel	pass
x86/smm_test			pvm	skip	no KVM_CAP_X86_SMM -- PVM stubs SMM
x86/smm_test			intel	pass

# --- real PVM differences, not yet explained --------------------------
# Each of these passes under kvm-intel in the same L1, on the same guest
# image, and fails under PVM.  They are recorded as expected failures so
# the suite is usable, not because they are acceptable.
#
# cr4_cpuid_sync_test: after the guest sets CR4.OSXSAVE, CPUID.1:ECX[27]
# still reads back clear.  Suggests PVM's CR4 write path does not run the
# runtime CPUID update.
x86/cr4_cpuid_sync_test		pvm	fail	OSXSAVE not reflected in CPUID after CR4 write
x86/cr4_cpuid_sync_test		intel	pass

# kvm_pv_test: writing MSR_KVM_SYSTEM_TIME triple faults the guest
# (KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN) where the test expects to reach its ucall.
x86/kvm_pv_test			pvm	fail	MSR_KVM_SYSTEM_TIME write triple faults
x86/kvm_pv_test			intel	pass

# userspace_msr_exit_test: msr_filter_allow expects KVM_EXIT_X86_RDMSR and
# gets KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN.  The other three subtests pass, so the filter
# itself works; what does not is the exit to userspace, which suggests
# PVM's MSR paths bypass kvm_msr_user_space().
x86/userspace_msr_exit_test	pvm	fail	MSR filter userspace exit does not happen
x86/userspace_msr_exit_test	intel	pass
